purpose: Reusable bright role colors for engineering report figures. Customer templates and accepted figures control any existing mapping.

baseline.meaning: Measured or modeled base state before the proposed allocation.

allocation.meaning: Actual saved allocation or its synchronized outcome.

comparison.meaning: Named comparator calculated on the same scope.

limit.meaning: Physical constraint or reference, with its true units.

nonnegative_margin.meaning: Zero is a binding capacity, increasing jade denotes more remaining capacity.

violation.meaning: A negative margin or an explicitly recorded infeasible condition.

available_unused.meaning: Available for allocation with a known zero assignment.

outside_window.meaning: Outside the allowed allocation window; distinguished by position and the availability outline.

selection_rules: Choose a small role-specific subset. A module number alone is not a color meaning.
Primary frames, text and connectors use structure. Color identifies scientific marks or the interiors of meaningful objects.
Use chromatic or open interiors for data marks, ink outlines and readable direct labels. Yellow or pale fills need an ink edge; use ink text against them.
Give categories marker, line or direct-label redundancy. Select sequential normalization for ordered magnitude and a meaningful signed pivot for differences.
Do not apply a palette to natural-color photographs or observational RGB pixels. A scalar physical field may use a documented shared physical display scale.
For new figures use the role palette when neither project identity nor the data define color. Keep previously accepted mappings when revising only content or export.
